claims.text: Adding empirical design parameters to machine-learning models improves phase prediction for high-entropy alloys.

The proposed model inputs include density estimate, enthalpy and entropy of mixing, melting-temperature estimate, valence-electron concentration, atomic-size difference, and differences in Pauling electronegativity.
Mixing entropy is physically relevant to phase constitution in high-entropy alloys.
The other listed empirical parameters are relevant physical or chemical predictors of phase constitution.
Phase distribution and microstructure mediate the effect of adding model descriptors on predictive performance.
Including the empirical parameters will improve melting-temperature and other melting-property prediction accuracy relative to current phase-prediction models.
Including the empirical parameters will make prediction of melting temperature and other melting properties more computationally efficient.
Machine-learning models currently exist for predicting phases in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed approach should remain valid for high-entropy alloys containing multiple principal elements.
The approach is limited or bounded for high-entropy alloys with simple compositions or limited data.
The effectiveness of the approach depends on the quality and quantity of training data.
